case.title: A raised phenylalanine on newborn screening
case.brief:
Referral from the newborn screening laboratory. A baby boy had a blood spot phenylalanine of 1,250 µmol/L on day 5. At 7 days his plasma phenylalanine was 1,480 µmol/L with a low tyrosine. His blood spot pterins and DHPR activity were normal, so BH4 deficiency is excluded.

PAH sequencing found two heterozygous variants: NM_000277.3:c.1222C>T p.(Arg408Trp) and NM_000277.3:c.1066-11G>A, which is in an intron. His mother carries the first and his father carries the second.
tasks: Are the two variants in trans? What do the parents’ results show, and how many PM3 points does this patient add?
c.1066-11G>A is not at a canonical splice site. What do SpliceAI and the literature say it does to splicing, and which criterion does that evidence go under?
Both variants are in gnomAD. Why doesn’t that count against them? Think about carriers of a recessive disorder.
Classify both variants and sign them, then compare with the ClinGen PKU expert panel.
case.source: The variants are NM_000277.3(PAH):c.1222C>T (GRCh38 12-102840493-G-A, CA251523, ClinVar VCV000000577) and NM_000277.3(PAH):c.1066-11G>A (GRCh38 12-102843790-C-T, CA251538, ClinVar VCV000000607). The classifications are the ClinGen PKU VCEP’s, from the Evidence Repository, checked in October 2026. The patient and family are fictional.

patients.ref: Case 3: a baby with a raised phenylalanine on newborn screening
patients.referral: Newborn blood spot screening found a phenylalanine of 1,250 µmol/L on day 5.
patients.summary: He was referred at 7 days old after newborn screening. His plasma phenylalanine was 1,480 µmol/L and his tyrosine was low. Blood spot pterins and dihydropteridine reductase (DHPR) activity were normal, so BH4 deficiency is excluded. He has been started on a phenylalanine-restricted diet.
patients.familyHistory: His parents are unrelated and both are well. His older sister is well and had a normal newborn screen. Parental testing shows that his mother carries c.1222C>T and his father carries c.1066-11G>A.

phenotypes.name: Hyperphenylalaninemia
phenotypes.note: Blood spot 1,250 µmol/L on day 5; plasma 1,480 µmol/L. BH4 deficiency excluded (normal pterins and DHPR).

patients.notes: The patient and family are fictional, but the variants and the published evidence about them are real.

expected.source: ClinGen Phenylketonuria expert panel (VCEP), Evidence Repository; ClinVar VCV000000577 (Pathogenic, reviewed by expert panel, 2018-08-06).

notes.PS3: Met, because expression studies show enzyme activity of about 1 to 2% of normal (PMIDs 25596310, 17935162).
notes.PM3: Met at a strong level using the panel’s points. The variant has been found in people with PKU both in trans with other pathogenic PAH variants and in the homozygous state. This patient adds another observation in trans, which his parents’ results confirm.
notes.PP3: The computational tools agree that it damages the protein.
notes.PP4: Met at moderate strength under the panel’s rule, because the phenylalanine level is typical of PKU and BH4 deficiency has been excluded.
notes.PM2: Not met, because the variant is at about 1 in 600 European alleles in gnomAD v4.1, which is above the panel’s PM2 threshold of 0.02%. Many pathogenic variants of recessive disorders are this common, because carriers are well. For comparison, the panel’s BS1 threshold is 0.2%.

expected.source: ClinGen Phenylketonuria expert panel (VCEP), Evidence Repository, specifications v2.0.0; ClinVar VCV000000607 (Pathogenic, reviewed by expert panel, 2024-12-30).

notes.PVS1: Met at a strong level, because RNA studies show the effect on splicing directly. The change creates a new splice acceptor, so in the published patients the mRNA has 9 extra bases between exons 10 and 11, with only traces of the normal product. This is an in-frame insertion of three amino acids. A liver sample from one of those patients had no enzyme activity (PMID 1769645).
notes.PM3: Met at a very strong level. The variant has been found compound heterozygous with known pathogenic PAH variants in at least 15 people with PKU, although the phase wasn’t confirmed for all of them. By the panel’s count that comes to 5.5 points (PMIDs 23500595, 8990013). This patient adds one more, and his parents’ results show that his variants are in trans.
notes.PP4: Met at moderate strength, because the phenylalanine levels are typical of PKU and BH4 deficiency has been excluded.
notes.PP3: The panel didn’t apply PP3, although SpliceAI predicts an acceptor gain (0.98). The same splicing effect is already counted under PVS1, with RNA evidence, and ClinGen’s splicing guidance doesn’t count it twice.
notes.PM2: Not met, because the variant is at about 3 in 10,000 alleles in gnomAD, which is above the panel’s threshold of 0.0002.
